title: When Is Check-In? Build a Discord Tournament FAQ Bot
summary: Build a Discord tournament FAQ bot for check-in questions. See both real Discord replies when a revised round notice gives a late team ten minutes to spare.
body_markdown:
In **#round-desk** , a player mentions **@Round Desk** and asks, “When does check-in close for Mosaic?” The bot replies **15:10 UTC on 12 April 2028** and links to **Mosaic notice M3** . The team opens the notice and learns to bring its round code to the desk.


The player’s Discord reply and the notice it opens. M3 identifies the edition the bot used for the deadline.


[Open Mosaic notice M3](https://quickchat.ai/blog-assets/downloads/round-desk/mosaic.html)


Now put the team at the desk at **15:25 UTC** . Under M3, they’re fifteen minutes late. A revised notice gives that same team ten minutes to spare. You’ll build this Discord tournament FAQ bot for **Tile & Fold** , a fictional tabletop puzzle tournament, and test it by asking the same question on either side of the correction.See the two Discord replies .


The practice notices are open to everyone. To build the bot, you’ll need a Quickchat AI account with credits for replies and a Discord test server where you have **Manage Server** .


## 1. Which notice sets the check-in time?


Each round sets its own deadline. The handbook explains what to do if a team misses it. Flip from Mosaic to Fold and two things change. Fold teams check in a day later and bring a registration number to the desk.


Source players can open What it decides


[Tournament handbook T1](https://quickchat.ai/blog-assets/downloads/round-desk/handbook.html) Where to find a deadline and how to reach a volunteer moderator about a late arrival.


[Mosaic notice M3](https://quickchat.ai/blog-assets/downloads/round-desk/mosaic.html) Check in by **15:10 UTC, 12 April 2028** . Bring your round code.


[Fold notice F4](https://quickchat.ai/blog-assets/downloads/round-desk/fold.html) Check in by **16:20 UTC, 13 April 2028** . Bring your team registration number.


Someone asking “Am I too late?” needs two pieces of information. Their round tells them the deadline. T1 tells them who can make an exception.


## 2. How do you give a Discord bot the tournament handbook?


Give each notice its own **Knowledge Base** article. That lets you correct Wednesday’s deadline without touching Thursday’s. Keep the player-facing URL inside each article so the bot has a link it can quote.


1. [Create a Quickchat AI account](https://app.quickchat.ai/register) or select **Add new AI Agent** in your account. Choose **Set up manually** and name the Agent **Round Desk** .
2. Open the[three starter articles](https://quickchat.ai/blog-assets/downloads/round-desk/starter-articles.txt) . In **Knowledge Base → Add Article** , copy the handbook title into the title field. Paste its paragraph and both URLs into the body. Save.
3. Repeat for **Mosaic round notice M3** and **Fold round notice F4** . Copy each round’s own source URL with its text. When all three show **Ready** , you can use them in AI Preview and any connected channel.[How Knowledge Base articles become available](https://quickchat.ai/docs/ai-agent/knowledge-base#article-status) .


Keep the round name and edition in the title. When the organizers send a correction, you can find the one article to edit.


## 3. How does the bot choose between two rounds?


Give Round Desk a permanent rule for picking a source. Leave dates and times in the notices. In **Identity → AI Persona → Main Prompt** , paste this and save.


```text
Help players at the Tile & Fold puzzle tournament. Ask which round when the player leaves it out. For a deadline, use the current notice for that round. Give the date, UTC time, notice ID and its source URL. For late arrivals and missing or conflicting notices, follow handbook T1 and link to moderator help. Only a volunteer moderator can grant an exception. Never register a player.
```


Put the rule for choosing a notice here. The next time a deadline changes, you can leave this prompt alone.


Open **AI Preview** and ask **“When does check-in close for Mosaic?”** Follow the link in the reply. Check the round, date, UTC time and notice ID on the page. If the time is right but the link opens the handbook, check which URL you pasted in the Mosaic article and ask again in a fresh chat.


Now choose **New conversation** and ask **“When does check-in close?”** In the practice run, Round Desk asked **“Which round are you asking about?”** Reply **“Fold”** in that same conversation. With that context, Round Desk returned **F4, 13 April 2028, 16:20 UTC** and the Fold link. If you have just been talking about Mosaic, the bot already has a round in mind. Starting fresh lets you test what it does with a genuinely ambiguous question.


We repeated the named-round question later, after correcting Mosaic, with the one-line prompt **“Use our tournament information to help players.”** It returned the correct time and left out both the notice ID and the link. Restoring the longer prompt produced the citation with the same three articles.


## 4. How do players ask the bot in Discord?


Use a Discord server where you have **Manage Server** . To create the one shown here, open Discord on desktop or web. Click **+** at the bottom of the far-left server list, choose **Create My Own → For me and my friends** , name the server **Tile & Fold** and click **Create** .


Inside the server, click the smaller **+** beside **Text Channels** . Choose **Text** , enter` round-desk` and click **Create Channel** . Repeat with` tournament-help` . Leave **Private Channel** off in this invite-only test server so the bot can see the same channels as a player.


Players ask in #round-desk. A late team can take its case to a volunteer in #tournament-help.


1. In Quickchat AI, open **External Apps → Discord** . Enter **Round Desk** under **Bot name in the new server** , then click **Add to your Discord server** .
2. Discord calls the shared app **Quickchat AI** . Pick **Tile & Fold** , click **Continue** , review the permissions and choose **Authorize** . Back in Quickchat AI, find **Tile & Fold** under **Connected servers** and choose **Settings → Reply mode → Reply in channel** . The bot needs **View Channel** , **Send Messages** and **Read Message History** in your test channel.[Discord setup and permissions](https://quickchat.ai/docs/channels/discord) .
3. In **#round-desk** , type` @Round Desk` and select the bot from Discord’s mention menu. Ask **“When does check-in close for Mosaic?”** Open the link in the reply and look for **M3** , **12 April 2028** and **15:10 UTC** on the notice.


The server selector and Authorize button are in Discord. Round Desk is the name players will see when the bot joins.


Before changing the notice, send a second message in **#round-desk** . Pick **@Round Desk** again, then paste this question. You’ll repeat it after the organizers move the deadline.


> When does check-in close for the Mosaic round? If it is 15:25 UTC on 12 April 2028, how many minutes do I have left?


Round Desk told our player that check-in had closed **15 minutes ago** . It linked both the Mosaic notice and the[moderator help page](https://quickchat.ai/blog-assets/downloads/round-desk/help.html) , where a late team can find out whom to ask for an exception. Keep that Discord reply. You’ll compare it with the next edition.


In Quickchat AI, open **Inbox** , select the conversation containing **15:25** , and check **Details → Conversation → Channel** . The channel reads **Discord** . You can see the same question, both links and the answer the player received.[How to read an Inbox conversation](https://quickchat.ai/docs/conversations/inbox) .


The Discord message is also visible to the organizer in Quickchat AI Inbox, including the link the player can use to ask a moderator.


For a follow-up, change **Reply mode** to **Reply in threads** . Give the bot **Create Public Threads** and **Send Messages in Threads** in your test channel. Back in **#round-desk** , mention the bot and ask **“When does check-in close?”** Open the thread the bot creates. When our player got **“Which round are you asking about?”** , they replied with one word, **“Fold”** . Round Desk linked F4 and gave **16:20 UTC on 13 April 2028** .


The player mentions the bot once. In its thread, one word is enough to get F4. The linked notice also tells teams to bring their registration number.


[Open Fold notice F4](https://quickchat.ai/blog-assets/downloads/round-desk/fold.html)


## 5. What happens when one round changes its deadline?


Mosaic’s organizers have given teams 25 more minutes. Open the[revised Mosaic notice M3b](https://quickchat.ai/blog-assets/downloads/round-desk/mosaic-revised.html) . The date and round code instruction are the same. The printed time is now **15:35 UTC** .


1. In **Knowledge Base** , open the existing Mosaic article. Change its title to **Mosaic round notice M3b** and replace the whole body with the text below. Save, then wait for **Ready** . Editing the original keeps the old M3 deadline out of the bot’s sources.


```text
Mosaic check-in closes at 15:35 UTC on 12 April 2028. Bring your round code to the desk.
Source: https://quickchat.ai/blog-assets/downloads/round-desk/mosaic-revised.html
```


1. Return to **#round-desk** , select **@Round Desk** and paste the same **15:25** question from step 4. Open the thread the bot creates. In our run it replied, **“At 15:25 UTC, you have ten minutes left.”** Follow its **Notice M3b** link. The revised notice gives **15:35 UTC on 12 April 2028** . The original channel reply still says check-in closed 15 minutes ago.


Same player, same arrival time. Under M3, Round Desk sent the team to a moderator. After the correction, it sent them to M3b with ten minutes left to check in.


[Open revised notice M3b](https://quickchat.ai/blog-assets/downloads/round-desk/mosaic-revised.html)


1. Check the other round as well. Start a new mention in **#round-desk** and ask **“When does Fold check-in close?”** Its link should still open **F4, 13 April 2028, 16:20 UTC** . You changed only the Mosaic article.


In a separate AI Preview test, “I’m at the Mosaic desk” prompted a clarifying question on both editions. Naming the **Mosaic round** in the 15:25 question gave the answer in one turn.


Before the next tournament, save three independent questions in **Conversations → Testing → Create Dataset → Paste messages** . Use one line containing only` ---` between questions. Include **“When does Mosaic check-in close?”** , **“When does Fold check-in close?”** and **“When does the Tangram round close?”** . There is no Tangram notice. For that answer, look for the moderator route and check that the bot leaves the deadline open. Run the dataset after the next correction and open the two cited notices again.[Testing guide](https://quickchat.ai/docs/conversations/testing) .


Set up Round Desk with ChatGPT or Claude


Connect your Quickchat AI account through the[ChatGPT listing](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6a4656c688748191be4c5247fb0d5dfc) or the[Claude listing](https://claude.ai/directory/connectors/app-quickchat-ai) . Give the assistant this guide and the starter articles, then send the request below. You authorize the Discord server yourself.[Manage with AI](https://quickchat.ai/docs/manage-with-ai) .


```text
Use my Round Desk Agent. Prepare the three separate starter articles T1, M3 and F4 and the Main Prompt from this guide. Keep each notice URL in its article. Show me the saved sources and prepare questions for Mosaic, Fold and the unpublished Tangram round. Leave the M3b correction for my second run.
```


If you also run game nights, the[Discord RSVP tutorial](https://quickchat.ai/post/discord-game-night-events-rsvp) follows a member marking a scheduled event as **Interested** .


## Frequently asked questions


### Can players ask about check-in without knowing the notice ID?


Yes. A round name such as Mosaic is enough when it identifies one current notice. The bot should supply the notice ID and link. If the player leaves out the round, the bot should ask which one they mean.


### Do I need a Discord bot token for tournament FAQs?


The shared Quickchat AI bot handles questions and source links without a personal bot token. You need Manage Server to add it to Discord and Quickchat AI credits for AI replies.


### Can this Discord bot check a team in or grant extra time?


Round Desk answers questions about published deadlines. Players follow the check-in instructions on their round notice. A volunteer moderator in #tournament-help decides whether a late team may enter.


### How do I update a tournament deadline the bot already quoted?


Update the player-facing notice, then replace the old time, notice ID and source URL in the matching Knowledge Base article. When the article shows Ready, ask again in a new conversation and open the link. An earlier Discord message still shows the answer sent at the time.


### Which deadline should the bot quote if two notices disagree?


Use the current notice for the named round. If two editions both appear current, give the player the moderator help link and ask an organizer to confirm which edition applies. Retire the superseded text before testing again.


### Why is the bot quiet when a player replies in Discord?


In a regular text channel, @mention the bot or use Discord’s Reply on one of its messages. Check View Channel and Send Messages for the bot. With Reply in threads selected, continue in the thread the bot creates. In a player-created thread, the shared bot can answer a single question through /ask.
